title.es: Dar la bienvenida a un recién llegado

es: Recibir a un recién llegado presentándole lugares y personas del barrio con cláusulas relativas y respondiendo a sus dudas.

teaching.en: Welcome to the neighbourhood! I am Sara, and I live next door.
teaching.es: ¡Bienvenido al barrio! Soy Sara y vivo al lado.
teaching.explanationEs: Welcome to + lugar es la fórmula para recibir a alguien.
segments: Welcome to the neighbourhood! I am
Sara, and I live next door.
teaching.audioText: Welcome to the neighbourhood! I am Sara, and I live next door.

teaching.en: Let me introduce you to Carlos, who has lived here for thirty years.
teaching.es: Déjame presentarte a Carlos, que lleva treinta años viviendo aquí.
teaching.explanationEs: Who has lived here añade un dato extra entre comas sobre alguien que ya nombras.
segments: Let me introduce you to Carlos, who
has lived here for thirty years.
teaching.audioText: Let me introduce you to Carlos, who has lived here for thirty years.

teaching.en: There is a good bakery nearby, which opens at six.
teaching.es: Hay una buena panadería cerca, que abre a las seis.
teaching.explanationEs: Which opens at six es un dato extra sobre la panadería; por eso va entre comas.
teaching.audioText: There is a good bakery nearby, which opens at six.

teaching.en: The pharmacy that you need is behind the library.
teaching.es: La farmacia que necesitas está detrás de la biblioteca.
teaching.explanationEs: That you need identifica cuál farmacia: no lleva comas.
teaching.audioText: The pharmacy that you need is behind the library.

teaching.en: Leo, whose workshop is on the next street, is very helpful.
teaching.es: Leo, cuyo taller está en la calle de al lado, es muy servicial.
teaching.explanationEs: Whose + nombre: el taller es de Leo; el dato va entre comas.

teaching.audioText: Leo, whose workshop is on the next street, is very helpful.

teaching.en: Every newcomer is invited to the square where we meet on Sundays.
teaching.es: Cada recién llegado está invitado a la plaza donde nos reunimos los domingos.
teaching.explanationEs: Where we meet identifica la plaza; is invited es una pasiva.
segments: Every newcomer is invited to the
square where we meet on Sundays.
teaching.audioText: Every newcomer is invited to the square where we meet on Sundays.

prompt.es: ¿Qué dos dudas tiene el recién llegado?

choices.text: A pharmacy and a bike repair.

feedback.es: El texto pregunta por una farmacia cercana y por quién puede arreglar una bici.

hint.es: Lee las dos preguntas del texto.

origin.text: Leo: Is there a pharmacy nearby? And who can repair my bike?

prompt.es: Completa: «El mercado donde compro fruta abre los sábados.»

feedback.es: Un lugar pide where: the market where I buy fruit.

hint.es: Se habla de un lugar: elige el relativo de lugar.

origin.text: The market ___ I buy fruit opens on Saturdays.

prompt.es: Elige la presentación correcta: «Te presento a Leo, que arregla bicis.»

choices.text: Let me introduce you to Leo, which repairs bikes.
Let me introduce you to Leo, who repairs bikes.
Let me introduce you to Leo, he repairs bikes.

feedback.es: Leo es una persona y el dato va entre comas: who repairs bikes. Which es para cosas y he no puede abrir una cláusula relativa.

hint.es: Es una persona y el dato va entre comas.

answer.text: Welcome to the neighbourhood where I live

feedback.es: Where I live identifica el barrio y cierra la frase de bienvenida.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué lugar necesita el recién llegado.

feedback.es: That you need identifica el lugar que necesita: la farmacia. Which opens at nine es un dato extra sobre la biblioteca.

origin.audio: The library, which opens at nine, is near the pharmacy that you need.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase de bienvenida con su traducción.

pairs: Let me introduce you to Carlos.
There is a good bakery nearby.

feedback.es: Son las frases útiles para recibir a alguien: saludo, presentación, recomendación y consejo.

pairs: Let me introduce you to Carlos.
There is a good bakery nearby.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase da un dato extra sobre un vecino ya presentado?

choices.text: Carlos, who lives next door, repairs bikes.
The man who lives next door repairs bikes.
The neighbour who repairs bikes is Carlos.

feedback.es: Las comas marcan el dato extra: Carlos ya está identificado. En las otras dos, la cláusula relativa es la que identifica al vecino.

prompt.es: Completa: «El día en que te mudas es el sábado.»

feedback.es: Un día es un momento, así que el relativo es when.

origin.text: Saturday is the day ___ you move into the house.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige a quién describe el audio.

feedback.es: Who repairs bikes es la pista que identifica: un mecánico. Whose workshop is behind the library solo añade su ubicación.

origin.audio: It is a person who repairs bikes, and whose workshop is behind the library.

prompt.es: Da la bienvenida a un vecino nuevo: presenta tres lugares, dos personas y responde.

answer.text: Welcome to the neighbourhood! The bakery that is on the corner opens at six, and the library, which is very quiet, is next to the square where we meet on Sundays. Sara, who lives next door, is very helpful, and Carlos, whose workshop is behind the library, repairs bikes. You asked about a pharmacy: the pharmacy that you need is nearby, behind the library too. Ask us if you have a question.
accepted: Welcome to the neighbourhood! The bakery that is on the corner opens at six, and the library, which is very quiet, is next to the square where we meet on Sundays. Sara, who lives next door, is very helpful, and Carlos, whose workshop is behind the library, repairs bikes. You asked about a pharmacy: the pharmacy that you need is nearby, behind the library too. Ask us if you have a question.

Welcome! The bakery which is on the corner opens at six. The library, which is very quiet, is next to the square where we meet on Sundays. Sara, who lives next door, can help you. Carlos, whose workshop is behind the library, is the person who repairs bikes. There is a pharmacy nearby, and it is behind the library. Please ask us if you need anything.

feedback.es: Un buen mensaje presenta lugares con that o where sin comas, personas con who o whose entre comas y responde con datos concretos a las dos dudas.

origin.text: Lugares: la panadería (en la esquina; abre a las seis), la biblioteca (muy tranquila; junto a la plaza), la plaza (donde nos reunimos los domingos). Personas: Sara (vive al lado) y Carlos (su taller está detrás de la biblioteca; arregla bicis). Preguntas del vecino: ¿hay una farmacia cerca? (sí, detrás de la biblioteca).

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase responde a «¿Dónde puedo comprar pan?»

choices.text: The bakery what I buy bread opens at six.
The bakery when I buy bread opens at six.
The bakery where I buy bread opens at six.

feedback.es: Un lugar pide where: the bakery where I buy bread. What y when no sirven como relativos de lugar.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige a qué hora abre el mercado.

feedback.es: El audio dice que el mercado donde compra fruta abre a las ocho. La farmacia solo se menciona para decir dónde está.

origin.audio: Welcome! The pharmacy that you need is behind the library, and the market where I buy fruit opens at eight.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Te presento a Leo, que vive cerca de aquí.»

answer.text: Let me introduce you to Leo, who lives nearby

feedback.es: Who lives nearby es un dato extra sobre Leo, por eso va entre comas.
